So it started off with me thinking I could just go to any auto shop and they would change my oil. I was wrong. I went to 3 different auto shops in my area (all of them said they could change motorcycle oil on google). So I said screw it and decided I'd do it myself. Then, I went to a auto supply store... SURPRISE SURPRISE they don't have the oil I need, nor the oil filter. They told me they could order it for me to which I responded with "I got it" and walked out. So I ordered that myself as well! It came in about a week later.

Now was the actual learning part. I had watched two videos on Youtube on how to change it so I was basically an expert. I had my friend over and he helped me with the whole process. We started off and we drained the oil no problem but one of the videos I watched said it was *possible* to get the oil filter off with your hand... It wasn't. So we rushed to the auto supply store 10 minutes before it closed and got an oil filter wrench. We couldn't figure out what size we needed because their sizing guide was awful, so we just did our best and headed home. We started using the wrench but it wouldn't grip right and kept sliding. I don't have many tools at my house but my friend does and he knew he could get it off if he had his tools but he live 30 mins away so we didn't wanna leave immediately.

Then, I had a brilliant idea. What solves all problems? Duct tape. I put Duct tape on the oil filter to give the wrench some grip and boom, it came right off. So then we just put on the new filter and put in the new oil and I was set! Hopefully next time it'll be a lot faster since I'll be prepared; however, it was a great learning experience and I'm glad I did it!
